title: India Beat Pakistan 5-3 in Hockey World Cup Thriller to Seal Next Round Spot
excerpt: Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored twice as India recovered from their England loss to beat Pakistan in a dramatic Group D finale at Amstelveen, eliminating their rivals and advancing to the second round.
body:
• India defeated Pakistan 5-3 in a high-scoring Hockey World Cup group stage thriller at the Wagener Stadion in Amstelveen, Netherlands, securing qualification for the second round.
  • Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored twice from penalty corners, while Abhishek netted two field goals and Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke for India's five goals.
  • Pakistan, who also lost 4-1 to England and drew 3-3 with Wales, have been eliminated from the tournament after finishing bottom of Group D.
  • India will carry their points into the second round alongside group toppers England, where they will be joined by the Netherlands and one of Argentina or New Zealand.

India extended their modern dominance over Pakistan with a commanding 5-3 victory at the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026 at the Wagener Stadion in Amstelveen on Wednesday, sealing their place in the second round while eliminating their arch-rivals from the tournament. Captain Harmanpreet Singh led from the front with two goals as India recovered from their 2-4 loss to England two days earlier with a performance that combined clinical finishing with stretches of breathtaking attacking hockey.

India Storm to Early Control

India left no room for doubt about their intentions from the opening whistle. Harmanpreet opened the scoring in the fifth minute with a trademark drag flick from the game's first penalty corner, blasting the ball into the bottom right corner. Six minutes later, Abhishek doubled the lead with a superb individual effort — dribbling his way past multiple defenders down the inside left channel in a display of close control that drew roars from the traveling Indian support.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=pIe3a2O93Kg

Harmanpreet struck again in the 21st minute, initially attempting a cheeky pass off a penalty corner before the ball was worked back to him for a powerful slap from close range. At 3-0, India looked in total command.

Pakistan Fight Back Before Half

Pakistan, who had managed just a 3-3 draw against Wales in their previous match, refused to fold. Hannan Shahid pulled one back just a minute after Harmanpreet's second, working a brilliant field goal through speed and close dribbling to make it 3-1. The 24th minute produced a chaotic passage of play with both teams scoring within moments: Abhishek added his second with a sensational piece of 3D skill in the goalmouth before Sufyan Khan smashed home a drag flick from Pakistan's first penalty corner to make it 4-2 at halftime.

"Press, counter, perform isn't just our tactical identity — it's how this group trains and thinks together every single day. We are not getting ahead of ourselves — one game at a time, all in, is the mentality we're taking into every match."

— Craig Fulton, India Head Coach

Hardik Seals It From the Spot

India started the third quarter with renewed intensity. Inside five minutes of the restart, a dangerous tackle by Pakistan's Arshad Liaqat on Sukhjeet Singh resulted in a penalty stroke. Hardik Singh stepped up and made no mistake, slotting the ball past the goalkeeper to put India 5-2 ahead and effectively end the contest.

Pakistan pulled one back through Hannan Shahid in the fourth quarter — his second goal of the match — but it was nothing more than a consolation. India's defensive structure held firm in the closing stages, denying Pakistan any real route back into the game.

World Cup Rivalry Renewed After 16 Years

The victory was India's first meeting with Pakistan at a Hockey World Cup since 2010 in New Delhi, where India won 4-1. Their World Cup rivalry, dating back to 1971, carries a weight that transcends the sport — and this edition was no different, with the emotional stakes amplified by India needing a result after their shock loss to England.

India's group-stage record reads: beat Wales 3-1, lost to England 2-4, beat Pakistan 5-3. England topped Group D with a perfect record after hammering Wales 8-2 earlier on Wednesday. Both India and England advance to the second round, where they will be joined by the Netherlands and one of Argentina or New Zealand from Group A.

What It Means for the Diaspora

India vs. Pakistan in any sport carries enormous weight for the diaspora, and hockey — the sport where this rivalry was born decades before cricket took center stage — hits differently. For NRI fans who remember the glory days of Indian hockey or who followed the team's resurgence at the 2023 Asian Games and the Paris Olympics, this result is both reassurance and fuel.

India's next challenge in the second round will be tougher. England and the Netherlands are genuine title contenders. But with Harmanpreet Singh continuing to convert penalty corners at an elite rate and attackers like Abhishek producing moments of individual brilliance, Craig Fulton's squad has the firepower to go deeper into this tournament.
